title: Ito events
description: Everything the server says on `GET /v0/events`. Each Server-Sent Event carries one event: its `id:` line is the event's id and its `data:` line is the event as JSON. Apps skip event types they don't recognise, but still keep their id as the cursor.

Event.description: One event on the stream; its `type` says which.

EventId.description: Opaque and never reused, even after the server is restored from a backup. Resume by sending the id of the last event you applied as `Last-Event-ID`.

MessageId.description: Opaque. The app makes the ids of the messages you send (random UUIDs); the server makes the ids of the agent's messages.

TurnId.description: Opaque. A turn is one run of the agent, from its inputs to an answer, a stop or an error.

StepId.description: Opaque. The server makes it when a step starts.

AskId.description: Opaque. The server makes it when the agent asks.

AttachmentId.description: Opaque: the `UploadId` the app made for what it uploaded, or an id the server made for a recording it keeps, such as a spoken message's.

FileId.description: Opaque: the id of a file Kumo showed you, which stays the same across its versions.

UploadId.description: A random UUID, in lowercase, the app makes before uploading. It is the attachment's id and its retry key.

CallId.description: A random UUID the app makes when you start a call.

Timestamp.description: Server time, RFC 3339 in UTC with milliseconds.

Position.description: Where a message or a step sits in the conversation: strictly increasing in conversation order, with gaps. Snapshots and history pages carry messages and steps in separate lists; merge them by position.

Outcome.description: How a message or a turn ended: `completed`; `stopped` by you; `interrupted` because the server restarted; or `failed`, with an error. A message alone may end `discarded`: the agent took it back unfinished, such as a reply whose model stream dropped and that the model writes again from the start, so hide it; snapshots and history leave it out. Treat an outcome you don't recognise as ended.

Error.description: Why something failed. A failed turn uses `model_timeout`, `model_unavailable`, `usage_limit`, `engine_signed_out`, `context_full`, `engine_failed`, `server_disk_full`, `refused` or `internal`. A refused command uses `invalid_request`, `token_rejected`, `pairing_code_rejected`, `not_found`, `id_conflict`, `too_large`, `attachment_missing`, `slow_down`, `unavailable` or `internal`. Codes are added over time: show the message of a code you don't recognise.

message.description: A plain sentence for the person using the app, written by the server.
examples: The model service isn't responding right now.

detail.description: The technical cause, for a Details view.

MessageKind.description: Agent messages only. A `reply` is part of the answer. A `note` is the agent's commentary while it works, such as "I'll check current prices first."; an app may show notes as live detail instead of in the conversation. A `post` is a message Kumo wrote outside a turn, such as how a mail it read changes your plans, or its first question while getting started. Hide a kind you don't recognise.

Message.description: One message, in the main chat or in a side thread. Messages are ordered by when they began, wherever they are.

role.description: `user` for what you send, `agent` for what the agent writes.

turn.description: Replies and notes only: the turn that wrote it.

text.description: GitHub-flavoured Markdown, exactly as written. While a message is still being written, the text so far. Empty for a message that only carries attachments, and for a reply that stands in for a turn that failed or was cut off before writing. A reply may hold `ari:` blocks, described in [the blocks schema](blocks.schema.json).

at.description: When the message began: when the server accepted it, or the agent's first word.

answers.description: User messages only: the ask this message answered. Any message you send while an ask waits answers it, whether or not you meant it to.

attachments.description: User messages only: the photos and files you attached, in order.

spoken.description: Only on a message you spoke on a call.

ended_at.description: Agent messages only: when it ended.

outcome.description: Agent messages only. Absent while the message is still being written.

urgent.description: Kumo's posts only: it couldn't wait, so its notification was time-sensitive and broke through your Focus. Absent otherwise.

done.description: User messages only: the Done entry this message replies to, such as a correction to one of Kumo's calls.

thread.description: The side thread it's in. Absent in the main chat.

quotes.description: User messages only: inside a thread, the message you replied to.

share.description: User messages only: on something you shared from your phone's share sheet, what you shared besides your note, which is the `text`, and the photos and files, which are the `attachments`. Kumo puts a share in the side thread it belongs in, or in a new one it names, and answers it there.

Shared.description: What you shared from your phone's share sheet, besides your note and its photos and files: a link, and text from another app.

text.description: Text you shared from another app, such as a passage you selected, exactly as it came.

SharedLink.description: A link you shared, with what the server read from the page where it could, so the app can show it as a card without going to the site.

url.description: The link, exactly as you shared it.

description.description: The page's summary of itself, as it gives one to link previews.

site.description: The site's name, such as "Halcyon Careers", or else its host.

AttachmentKind.description: `image` for a JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP photo, which the agent sees; `audio` for a recording, such as a spoken message's or one you send, which the server transcribes for the agent; `file` for anything else, which lands in the agent's workspace. Treat a kind you don't recognise as a file.

Attachment.description: A photo or file you attached to a message. Its bytes never change: fetch them once with `GET /v0/attachments/{attachment}` and keep them.

media_type.description: The media type it was uploaded with, such as `image/jpeg`.

width.description: Images only: in pixels, when the server could read it.

height.description: Images only: in pixels, when the server could read it.

StepKind.description: What kind of thing the agent did. `handoff` and `commit` are written by the server, not the agent: a time Kumo's browser needed your hand, and how a one-tap card you answered went. Show the title of a kind you don't recognise.

Step.description: One thing the agent did while working on a turn: thinking, a web search, a command, an edit, a tool, a plan, a wait. Its title is plain words written by the server, safe to show as it is. Its other fields carry the specifics exactly as the agent used them (commands, paths, queries, URLs, output); show what you choose. Fields beyond the common ones belong to particular kinds, and a step carries those its kind has.

turn.description: The turn the step belongs to.

title.description: Plain words, such as "Reading notes.md": present tense while the step runs, past tense once it has completed ("Read notes.md"). A step that didn't complete keeps its present-tense title.

ended_at.description: When the step ended. Absent while it runs.

outcome.description: How the step ended. Absent while it runs. `completed`: it ran, whatever its result; a command that exits non-zero, such as a search that finds nothing, is completed, with its `exit_code`. `failed`: it couldn't run, or a tool reported an error. `stopped` or `interrupted`: its turn was stopped, or cut off by a restart.

duration_ms.description: How long the step took, once it has ended.

heading.description: `thinking`: the heading the model gave its reasoning.

summary.description: `thinking`: the model's summary of its reasoning, as far as it has been written.

queries.description: `web_search`: every query, when there were several.

url.description: `web_search`: the page opened or searched within. `tool`: what the tool made, such as the issue a report opened or added to.

pattern.description: `web_search`: the words looked for on a page.

results.description: `web_search`: results, when the search returned them.

command.description: `command`: the command line, exactly as run.

actions.description: `command`: what the command did, as far as the engine could tell: read a file, search for a term, list a folder, or run something else.

exit_code.description: `command`: its exit code, once it has ended. Non-zero doesn't make the step failed.

output.description: `command`: the end of what it printed, at most the last 2 KB, once it has ended.

from.description: For a moved file, where it was.

capability.description: `tool`: the capability the tool belongs to, such as a server's name.

arguments.description: `tool`: the arguments it was called with, as JSON.

detail.description: What went wrong, in the tool's or command's own words, when the step failed.

action.description: `memory`: `used` for the pages Ari drew on in this turn (one step, growing as it reads), `updated` for a page it wrote, `journaled` for an addition to today's journal. `motion`: `started`, `updated`, `finished`, `restored` or `forgotten`, for what Ari did to the thing.

pages.description: `memory`: the pages, by address and title, never their content. Past conversations show as one entry with the address `conversation:past`.

change.description: `memory` with `updated`: the change to fetch from `GET /v0/memory/changes/{change}` when someone taps it.

motion.description: `motion`: the thing Ari started or changed. Open it with `GET /v0/motion/{motion}`.

version.description: `motion`: the thing's version after the change.

note.description: `motion`: Ari's note on the change, such as "Booked the Uffizi, 8:15 Saturday". `tool`: why, in a line, such as the reason a mail was binned.

tally.description: `tool`: what this step did in a word or two, for counting a run of steps like it, such as `binned` or `into Money & receipts`.

run_title.description: `tool`: how a run of steps of the same operation reads as one line, with `{count}` for how many: `present` while one of them runs, `past` once they're over, such as "Sorted {count} mails". Each step still has its own title. Absent for a tool whose steps don't share a line.

mails.description: `tool`: the mails the step read, found or moved, so it can open onto them rather than their ids: at most 50, in the order the step gave them. A mail it read carries its `text`, cut at a few thousand characters, with `cut` when there was more.

from.description: The sender's name, or address when there's no name.

text.description: The mail as plain text, without the quoted history.

cut.description: Present when `text` stops short of the whole mail.

explanation.description: `plan`: why the plan is what it is.

items.description: `plan`: its items, in order, each with its state.

wait_ms.description: `wait`: how long the agent chose to wait.

handoff.description: `handoff`: a time Kumo's browser needed your hand, or you took the page over, kept in the trail of the thread its task lives in so it outlasts a relaunch. Its `title` says what for, such as "Needed you to log in", or "You took over" when Kumo hadn't asked; draw `answer` under it, such as "You logged in and handed back · 17:21". It ends at once, as it's written, and `step.updated` adds the answer when the page comes back, even after its turn has ended.

need.description: What Kumo asked your hand for. Absent when you took the page over without being asked.

why.description: What Kumo asked, in its words, such as "Sign in to Railway so I can get the tickets".

answer.description: How the page came back: `handed_back` by you, `lapsed` when you left it untouched until it went back by itself, or `stopped` when you stopped the task. Absent while Kumo still waits on you, or you still hold the page. Treat one you don't recognise as handed back.

commit.description: `commit`: how a one-tap card you answered went, kept in the trail of the thread its task lives in, so the card can be drawn as it settled after it has left the Desk and after a relaunch. Its `title` says it in a line, such as "Pressed “Book now”". When Kumo settles an uncertain press, or reads the site's reference on the confirmation page, `step.updated` brings the new `outcome` or the `reference`.

card.description: The card, as it was on the Desk.

title.description: The card's title, such as "Table for two at Kiln".

verb.description: The card's option that acts, such as "Book".

answer.description: `declined`: what you tapped or wrote instead, such as "Not now".

reference.description: `done`: the site's reference for it, as Kumo read it on the confirmation page, such as "TW-48KQ". Absent until Kumo reads one, and when the site gave none.

page.description: The card's page as you saw it: its picture, summary and details.

AskKind.description: `question` asks for information or a choice. `approval` asks before the agent does something consequential, and shows a `preview` of what would happen. Treat a kind you don't recognise as a question.

AskOption.description: A suggested answer. Tapping it sends its `label` as your message.

label.description: A short answer, in plain words.

description.description: A little more about the option, when the agent gave it.

acts.description: Approvals only: present on the one option that goes ahead with the action, such as "Book it".

AskOutcome.description: How an ask ended: `answered` by a message, or `cancelled` by you before you answered, or because the agent asked something else. Treat an outcome you don't recognise as ended.

Ask.description: Something the agent asked you. Asking ends the agent's turn, and the ask waits as long as it takes: through the app closing, the phone going offline and the server restarting. The next message you send where it waits answers it, whether you tap an option, type your own answer or write about something else. At most one ask waits in each thread, and one in the main chat.

question.description: Plain words, written by the agent.

options.description: Suggested answers, in order. Empty when only a typed answer makes sense. An approval has options, and exactly one of them `acts`.

allows_text.description: Whether to offer a typed answer beside the options. Always true when there are no options.

preview.description: Approvals only: what would happen, in plain text, to show before you agree.

attachments.description: Approvals only: pictures that would leave the box if you agree, such as a report's screenshots, to show with the preview. Fetch each with `GET /v0/attachments/{attachment}`.

ended_at.description: When it was answered or cancelled.

answer.description: Present when the outcome is `answered`: the message that answered it.

thread.description: The side thread it waits in; absent for the main chat.

StatusKind.description: Coarse, for animating the agent's presence. Show the label of a kind you don't recognise.

StatusLabel.description: Plain words written by the server, safe to show as they are. While a step runs, its title.

StatusDetail.description: Optional plain-word specifics, such as a search query.

Status.description: What the agent is doing right now.

LiveTurn.description: The turn running when a snapshot was taken.

inputs.description: The messages the turn started with.

read.description: Messages sent while it was running that the agent has since taken in.

retry_of.description: Present when the turn is a new attempt at a failed one.

started_at.description: When the turn started, as in its `turn.started`, so an app can say how long the agent has been working. A turn is never failed for being quiet, so this is what tells you when it has gone on too long. Absent when the server no longer knows.

status.description: The current live status, if there is one yet.

thread.description: The side thread it answers in; absent for the main chat.

Snapshot.title: snapshot
Snapshot.description: The first event when the server can't resume from your cursor: there was none, the server doesn't know it (it was restored from a backup, compacted it away, or is a different server), or you are too far behind. Replace your view of the conversation and of the Desk with it. Its id is the id of the latest event, so resuming after it continues from here; it has no id while the conversation is empty.

reason.description: Why there was no replay: `no_cursor`, `cursor_unknown` or `too_far_behind`.

messages.description: The main chat's latest messages, oldest first, including a message still being written (with its text so far and no outcome). A thread's messages come with `GET /v0/threads/{thread}`; page further back with `GET /v0/messages`.

steps.description: Every step in the main chat from the first of these messages on, including the running turn's steps, in position order.

asks.description: Every ask in the main chat from the first of these messages on, in position order, including the one that waits for your answer (it has no outcome).

turn.description: The main chat's running turn, or null when it's idle. A thread's running turn comes with the thread.

next.description: Messages waiting as Next in the main chat, in the order they will be answered.

calls.description: The calls that started within these messages, and one still on.

threads.description: Every open thread, and every thread whose line sits among these messages, in position order.

onboarding.description: Present until getting started is done.

problems.description: What's wrong on the server right now, while anything is. Absent when nothing is.

browser.description: Kumo's browser, while it's doing something: browsing, waiting on you, or in your hands. Absent while it's idle.

access.description: How Kumo runs on the server, while it has full access. Absent while it runs in its sandbox.

MessageAccepted.title: message.accepted
MessageAccepted.description: A message you sent is on the server's disk. Every connected app receives it, the sender included.

MessageAmended.title: message.amended
MessageAmended.description: On a call you carried on speaking before Ari began to answer, so your words joined the message you'd just spoken. It carries the whole message as it is now: the text with your new words, and one recording of both parts, in place of the earlier recording, which is gone. Replace the message you have with it.

MessageQueued.title: message.queued
MessageQueued.description: The message can't join the running turn, so it waits as Next. It starts the turn after this one, together with any other waiting messages.

turn.description: The running turn it waits behind.

MessageRead.title: message.read
MessageRead.description: The agent has taken the message into the running turn. It reads new input at its next step, between model calls, so a reply it was already writing may finish first.

TurnStarted.title: turn.started
TurnStarted.description: The agent starts working. Stop works from this moment.

inputs.description: The messages this turn answers, in the order they were sent.

retry_of.description: Present when this is a new attempt at a failed turn.

thread.description: The side thread this turn answers in, with its own conversation. Absent for the main chat. Turns in different threads run at the same time.

TurnStatus.title: turn.status
TurnStatus.description: What the agent is doing now. It replaces the previous status, and `turn.ended` clears it.

StepStarted.title: step.started
StepStarted.description: The agent starts a step. It carries the step as it begins, with its present-tense title.

StepUpdated.title: step.updated
StepUpdated.description: More is known about a running step, such as more of its summary or its plan's progress. It carries the step as it now stands; replace your copy.

StepEnded.title: step.ended
StepEnded.description: A step ends. It carries the step as it finished: its outcome, duration, past-tense title, and what is known at the end.

MessageStarted.title: message.started
MessageStarted.description: The agent begins a message: its text is empty and it has no outcome yet. `message.delta` events follow.

MessageDelta.title: message.delta
MessageDelta.description: Text appended to a message. Text is never revised: `offset` is always the message's length before this piece.

offset.description: Where this piece starts, in UTF-16 code units.

thread.description: The side thread its message is in; absent in the main chat.

MessageEnded.title: message.ended
MessageEnded.description: A message is finished. Its final text is its first `length` UTF-16 code units: everything streamed, or less when you stopped it, cut where it was on your screen. Its `ended_at` is this event's `at`.

length.description: The final length of the text, in UTF-16 code units.

thread.description: The side thread its message is in; absent in the main chat.

AskStarted.title: ask.started
AskStarted.description: The agent asks you something. The turn that asked ends next; the ask waits for your answer.

AskEnded.title: ask.ended
AskEnded.description: The ask is settled: a message answered it, or it was cancelled. It carries the ask as it ended. When a message answers it, `message.accepted` for that message comes first.

TurnEnded.title: turn.ended
TurnEnded.description: The turn is over and its status is cleared. Nothing more about this turn follows.

MemoryPageRef.description: A page in memory, named but not shown.

MemoryAddress.description: Where something lives in memory: `memory:portrait`, `memory:now`, `memory:helping-you`, a shelf page such as `memory:people/alex`, a journal day such as `memory:journal/2026-10-25`, a thing in motion such as `motion:florence-with-mira`, or `conversation:past`.

ChangeId.description: An opaque id the server chooses for one change to memory.

Call.description: A call with Ari, shown in the conversation as a block that opens and closes the stretch it covered.

position.description: Where the call started in the conversation.

ended_at.description: When it ended. Absent while it's on.

duration_ms.description: How long it lasted, once it has ended.

audio_deleted.description: True once you've deleted the audio of its spoken messages.

end_reason.description: Why the server ended it, in a line to show, such as "The connection dropped." Absent when you ended it.

ThreadId.description: Opaque. The server makes it when a side thread starts.

Quote.description: The message you replied to inside a thread, and the words of it to show above yours.

text.description: A line of the quoted message, at most 200 characters, safe to show as it is.

ThreadNews.description: Something Kumo said in a thread that you haven't seen yet.

text.description: Its first line, with Markdown stripped, at most 200 characters.

ThreadDone.description: Who marked a thread done, and when.

by.description: `kumo` when Kumo closed it because its question was answered or its task finished; `you` when you marked it.

Thread.description: A side thread: a subject of its own beside the main chat, with its own conversation, so talking in it never steers the main chat or another thread aside. Kumo starts one for a one-off, a new subject or long work, moving the message that started it in; you start one by replying to a message in the main chat, or from Threads. It shows in the main chat as one quiet line.

title.description: One to five plain words, such as "Kiln menu", safe to show as it is. Absent until Kumo names a thread you started, just after its first answer.

state.description: `open` while its question or task is still live; `done` once it's settled. Any message in a done thread opens it again.

position.description: Where its line sits in the main chat: just after the main chat's message with the greatest position below it. It moves to the end when Kumo comes back to the thread with something new.

anchor.description: A thread you started by replying to a message in the main chat: that message, which stays in the main chat with the thread's line under it while the line hasn't moved.

replies.description: How many messages it holds, yours and Kumo's, notes aside.

result.description: Kumo's one line on where it stands or how it ended, such as "Noodles, laab, skewers · £47 for two". Absent until Kumo writes one.

picture.description: Its first picture, yours or one Kumo found, for a thumbnail: fetch it with `GET /v0/attachments/{attachment}`.

page.description: It holds a page Kumo made: one of its replies or posts shows an `ari:made` card.

ThreadStarted.title: thread.started
ThreadStarted.description: A side thread starts: Kumo branched one, you replied to a message in the main chat, or you started one from Threads. A thread Kumo branches arrives before the messages it moves in.

ThreadChanged.title: thread.changed
ThreadChanged.description: Something about a thread changed: its name, whether it's open or done, its line's place in the main chat, how many replies it has, its result, its picture or its news. Replace your copy with this one.

MessageMoved.title: message.moved
MessageMoved.description: A message moved between the main chat and a thread, or between threads: Kumo branched a thread from it, or you moved it. It keeps its id and its position; `message` is the whole message as it is now, so an app that hadn't loaded where it came from can show it where it went.

from.description: The thread it left; absent when it left the main chat.

Spoken.description: How a message you spoke on a call came to be: the call, and its audio while it's kept.

audio.description: The recording of what you said. Absent once you've deleted the call's audio.

CallStarted.title: call.started
CallStarted.description: You started a call with Ari. While it's on, Ari speaks.

CallEnded.title: call.ended
CallEnded.description: The call ended, with how long it lasted.

CallAudioDeleted.title: call.audio_deleted
CallAudioDeleted.description: The audio of a call's spoken messages is deleted; their text stays.

VoiceState.description: Whether the server can hold a call: `ready` once it can both listen and speak, with memory's vocabulary loaded; `loading` while it starts; `failed` when it can't, until the server restarts.

VoiceReason.description: Why the voice isn't `ready`, in a plain line to show, such as "The GPU ran out of memory loading the voice."

VoiceStatus.title: voice.status
VoiceStatus.description: The server's voice changed. Offer Talk only while it's `ready`, and otherwise show the reason. It's sent on each change after the server starts; `GET /v0/voices` has the state at any time.

MotionId.description: A thing's id: readable, chosen by Ari, unique on the server, such as `florence-with-mira`.

Motion.description: A thing in motion: something going on that Kumo keeps for you, such as a trip being planned or a role you're interviewing for. Its content and state come from `GET /v0/motion/{id}`.

kind.description: Which widget draws it, and which section of In motion it sits in: `career`, `body`, `trip`, `project`, `learning` or `other`, always in that order. 0.18's `training` sits in Body, `pursuit` in Career, and `occasion` and `case` in Other until Kumo reshapes them. Show a kind you don't recognise as a plain card in Other.

title.description: Short, such as "Florence with Mira": Ari keeps it to 28 characters or fewer.

summary.description: Kumo's line for you: where it stands, short, such as "Virtual 1 · Python PR review" or "6–9 Nov · 3 to book". Kumo keeps it current with every change, and keeps sources, guesses and ids out of it, in the content's notes. Once it's finished, it says how it ended, such as "No offer after the final round".

status.description: `done` once Kumo stops keeping it: tracking ended, which isn't the same as achieving it. `outcome` says how it ended. A trip is done by itself once its last day is over where it happens, with no `outcome` until Kumo gives it one.

pinned.description: Whether it's pinned above the composer. Ari pins a thing it starts, unpins it when it's done or when you ask, and pins it again when you ask.

salience.description: How much it matters to you now, by Kumo's judgement of the stakes, the timing and what you've said, never by its stage or date: `loud` is big and carries the picture in its section, `normal` is a row, and `quiet` folds into "+ N quieter". You correct it by telling Kumo. Show a value you don't recognise as `normal`.

cover.description: The content's cover photo, for the card. Absent when it has none.

version.description: How many times it has changed, counting its start as 1.

done_at.description: When it was finished. Absent while it's active.

outcome.description: How it ended, once it's done: `achieved`; `not_met`, a goal missed; `let_go`, stopped by choice; `merged` into another thing; or one never to show, kept only to recover: `duplicate`, a copy of another thing, `test`, and `elsewhere`, small admin that lives on the Desk and in Kumo's plans now. Absent for a thing finished before 0.19, or a trip that ended by itself, until Kumo gives it one: show it as ended, never as achieved. Show a value you don't recognise as ended.

merged_into.description: For `merged` and `duplicate`: the thing it went into, to open.

position.description: The position of your message Ari was answering when it started the thing.

note.description: Ari's note, such as "Booked the Uffizi, 8:15 Saturday".

position.description: The position of your message Ari was answering when it made the change: link back to it.

MotionStarted.title: motion.started
MotionStarted.description: Ari started a thing in motion. Its `change` is the first entry of "What changed".

change.description: This change, as it appears in "What changed".

MotionChanged.title: motion.changed
MotionChanged.description: Ari changed a thing, or brought back an earlier version of it. Fetch its content again.

change.description: This change, as it appears in "What changed".

MotionFinished.title: motion.finished
MotionFinished.description: Ari finished a thing: it moves to Done.

change.description: This change, as it appears in "What changed".

MotionStateChanged.title: motion.state
MotionStateChanged.description: A thing's state changed, from a tap on any device, or because a change removed an item it named. It carries the whole state.

state.description: The whole state, as `motion.schema.json` describes for its kind.

MotionRemoved.title: motion.removed
MotionRemoved.description: You allowed Ari to forget a thing, so it's gone.

Picture.description: A picture Ari found on the web, kept on the server as an attachment so the app never contacts its host. Never generated.

source_url.description: The page the picture came from.

credit.description: Who made it, as its source asks.

MadeItemId.description: Lowercase words and dashes, unique on the page, such as `trajans-column`.

MadeState.description: Your ticks on a made page: when you ticked each item, by its id. `{}` until you tick something.

MadeId.description: A made page's id: readable, chosen by Ari, unique on the server, such as `va-guide`.

Made.description: A page Ari made: a rich, lasting answer, such as a gallery guide, that a reply shows as an `ari:made` card, and that sits on the Made shelf. Ari keeps it current. Its content and your ticks come from `GET /v0/made/{id}`.

title.description: Such as "Your guide to the V&A".

summary.description: What's in it, in one line, such as "4 rooms · 9 things to spot".

cover.description: The picture at its top and on its card. Absent when it has none.

for_day.description: The day it's for, such as the visit, as `YYYY-MM-DD`: "Made for Saturday". Ari keeps it current until then. Absent when it isn't for a day.

version.description: How many times it has changed, counting its making as 1.

changed_at.description: When Ari last changed it: "Updated 2h ago", with the latest change's note.

position.description: The position of your message Ari was answering when it made the page: "From your chat" links back to it.

thread.description: The side thread it was made in: "From your thread" opens it, with its name. Absent when it was made in the main chat.

MadeChange.description: One change to a made page.

note.description: What changed, said to you, such as "The Raphael Cartoons reopened this morning, so they're back in."

position.description: The position of your message Ari was answering when it made the change.

MadeCreated.title: made.created
MadeCreated.description: Ari made a page. It joins the Made shelf.

MadeChanged.title: made.changed
MadeChanged.description: Ari changed a page, such as when something on it changed in the world. Fetch its content again. It never notifies: when you need to know, Ari says so in a message.

MadeStateChanged.title: made.state
MadeStateChanged.description: Your ticks on a page changed, from a tap on any device, or because a change removed an item you'd ticked. It carries the whole state.

MadeRemoved.title: made.removed
MadeRemoved.description: You allowed Ari to forget a page, so it's gone from the shelf and its cards.

MessagePosted.title: message.posted
MessagePosted.description: Kumo posted a message into the conversation outside any turn, a `post`. It arrives whole, and it notifies every registered device.

CardId.description: Opaque. The server makes it for each card.

DoneId.description: Opaque. The server makes it for each entry.

WakeUpId.description: Opaque. The server makes it when a wake-up is set.

DreamId.description: Opaque. The server makes it when a dream finishes.

CalendarItemId.description: Opaque. The server makes it for each event it shows.

When.description: An instant, such as `2026-11-12T14:00:00Z`, or for an all-day event a date, such as `2026-11-12`.

CalendarItem.description: An event on one of your calendars, as the box reads it from iCloud. Open it with the event whose `uid` matches, in Apple's own views.

uid.description: The event's iCalendar UID, which finds it on the phone.

calendar.description: Which calendar it's on. `kumo` is true for Kumo's own calendar of holds, travel and prep.

leave_at.description: When to leave to get there on time, when Kumo worked it out.

motion.description: The thing in motion it belongs to, such as the Florence trip.

status.description: `hold` for a time Kumo is keeping free, `tentative` for maybe, `confirmed` otherwise.

guess.description: Only on Kumo's guesses at your day, on its own calendar: draw it as a guess, with why on a tap, and answer it with `POST /v0/desk/guesses/{item}/answer`. Kumo's plan for your day (a run, prep, a proper lunch, winding down) is on its calendar too, without it.

overlap.description: Only on Kumo's blocks it put over something else on purpose, such as a soft plan beside a call that's only held. Show what it overlaps, and why on a tap.

Overlap.description: Why Kumo's block overlaps something on purpose, and how you'll settle it. Each item keeps its own status: a hold stays a hold.

reason.description: In a line, such as "Both stand until Dana confirms the call; the walk gives way if it's on."

Guess.description: Kumo's guess at what you're doing then, from your past weeks, what you've said and what it can see. Once you've answered it, it's no longer a guess.

why.description: Why Kumo thinks so, in a line, such as "Your usual weekday at the desk, from the last four weeks."

Activity.description: What you're doing, in Kumo's picture of your day: `people` is seeing people, and `other` anything else, named in the title. Show one you don't recognise by its title.

CardAnswer.description: Your answer to a card: one of `option`, `slots` or `text`.

option.description: The label of the option you tapped.

slots.description: `times` cards: the indexes of the slots that are clear, in the card's order.

text.description: A typed answer; for a draft, the change you want.

Card.description: Something waiting on you on the Desk. It stays until it's done, or until it can no longer help: a card with `until`, or an invite once its event is over, leaves by itself then. Draw its buttons from `options`; `allows_text` offers a typed answer, which for a draft asks for a change, such as "a bit more casual". Its kind's payload sits under a field of the same name. Show a kind you don't recognise by its title and options.

at.description: When it began waiting, for "since Wed".

until.description: When it stops mattering, such as the evening a question about where to meet is for: it leaves the Desk by itself then. Absent for a card that waits however long it takes.

changed_at.description: When Kumo last changed it while it waited, such as rewriting a draft or bringing it back after it couldn't act. Absent if it hasn't changed. Mark a card whose `changed_at`, or `at` for a new one, is later than your last look at the Desk.

title.description: One line, such as "Draft to Tess".

state.description: `working` while the box acts on your answer, such as rewriting a draft. Absent while it waits on you.

answer.description: `working` only: the answer you gave, as you gave it, to show while the box acts.

draft.description: A reply Kumo wrote into your Drafts folder. Kumo never sends it: open it in Mail with `message://` and the draft's Message-ID, and send it yourself.

account.description: The mail account it's in, such as `icloud` or `outlook`.

body.description: The mail's words in light Markdown (paragraphs, bold, italics, lists and links), as it's formatted in Drafts: draw it formatted. A picture in it, written `![what it shows](…)`, is listed in `attachments`; leave it out of the words.

message_id.description: The draft's own Message-ID, without angle brackets.

in_reply_to.description: The Message-ID of the mail it answers.

signature.description: Their own signature, as plain text, learned from the mail they send from this account and added at the end. Draw it quietly under the words. Absent when they have none or asked for none.

attachments.description: The pictures it shows inline and the files attached, in order. Absent when there are none.

kind.description: `image` or `file`. Show a kind you don't recognise as a file.

inline.description: Shown in the mail's words rather than attached.

invite.description: An invitation, held on Kumo's calendar until you answer; your answer goes back through iCloud.

times.description: Times to check against your work calendar, which Kumo can't see. Answer with the slots that are clear.

question.description: Something Kumo isn't sure about, such as whether a mail it binned was right.

offer.description: Kumo offers to take something on, such as a need that keeps coming up. Accepting lets Kumo do it in the background.

CommitCard.description: A free booking or form Kumo has ready on a site, such as a table for two, for your one tap. Show the picture, the summary and the details, with the options: the one that `acts` has the box press the site's own button, exactly the one outlined in the picture, but only if the page is still as it was; if it changed, nothing is pressed and Kumo looks again. The other option, or words of your own, press nothing: Kumo hears them. Money never goes this way: where money moves, Kumo asks you to take over and press the button yourself.

url.description: The page's address, without its query.

button.description: The site's own button that a go-ahead presses, as it reads, such as "Book now".

summary.description: What pressing it does, in Kumo's words.

details.description: What matters, such as when, for how many, and the name it's under. Absent when Kumo gave none.

screenshot.description: The page as Kumo left it, at iPhone size, with the button outlined. Fetch it with `GET /v0/attachments/{attachment}`.

thread.description: The side thread the task lives in, where Kumo tells you how it went. Absent for the main chat.

CommitOutcome.description: How a one-tap card settled. `done`: the box pressed the site's button and the site answered. `uncertain`: it pressed, but the site's answer was lost, and Kumo checks on the site before anything is pressed again. `failed`: Kumo checked an uncertain press and it didn't go through. `changed`: the page had moved on before your tap, so nothing was pressed. `declined`: you said not now, or asked for a change, so nothing was pressed. `refused`: nothing was pressed, such as because money moves there or you held the page. Treat one you don't recognise as `refused`.

Desk.description: Home: Kumo's line and mood, the weather around you, Kumo's plans, what's coming up, what's waiting on you, how much Kumo handled today and when it last read your mail.

line.description: Absent until Kumo sets one, or after it clears it.

ambient.description: Absent while the box doesn't know roughly where you are, or couldn't read the weather lately.

plans.description: Kumo's plans: every wake-up, soonest first. Kumo setting one is quiet; it only shows here.

coming_up.description: Events in the next 36 hours or so, plus anything big this week, in time order.

waiting.description: Cards waiting on you, oldest first.

handled.description: How many things Kumo did without you today, local time: the Done entries that aren't `quiet`, for "Done · handled 9".

last_mail_at.description: When Kumo last read a new mail, for "Reading · last mail 2 min ago". Absent while no mail account is connected, and until the first mail.

DeskLine.description: Something interesting at the top of the Desk, by Kumo's judgement: its mood, how something's going, a thought, the day around you. It changes when the moment does, and it never notifies.

text.description: A short line, such as "Quiet morning. Your Northwind prep is two-thirds done."

mood.description: How Kumo feels, for its face: known moods are `bright`, `calm`, `cosy`, `focused`, `drowsy`, `proud` and `concerned`. Show one you don't recognise as `calm`.

Ambient.description: The weather where you roughly are, read on the box from Open-Meteo every half hour or so.

condition.description: `clear`, `partly_cloudy`, `cloudy`, `fog`, `drizzle`, `rain`, `snow` or `thunder`. Show one you don't recognise as `cloudy`.

place.description: Where, when the phone named it, such as "Rome".

DeskChanged.title: desk.changed
DeskChanged.description: Something on the Desk changed. It carries the whole Desk, which is small: replace yours.

DoneEntry.description: One thing Kumo did without you, for the Done list. Reply to it with a message whose `done` names it, and the correction becomes a preference.

text.description: What Kumo did, such as "Unsubscribed from Deliveroo promos and binned 3".

event.description: The event it added or changed.

quiet.description: A mail Kumo read and left alone: "read, nothing needed". Fold these into one line a day.

corrected_at.description: When you said it was wrong, with `POST /v0/done/{entry}/wrong`. Show it as noted rather than offering That was wrong again.

track.description: The track this call belongs to, when it's in an area Kumo is learning. "That was wrong" on it steps the track back.

dream.description: The dream that did it: show it with that dream rather than as the day's work. It doesn't count in the Desk's `handled`.

TrackId.description: Opaque. The server makes it when Kumo opens a track.

TrackStage.description: How far Kumo has come in an area: `learning`, it shows you its calls and asks when unsure; `spot_checks`, it checks with you now and then; `trusted`, it brings only what needs you. Draw it as three bars filled to the stage; show one you don't recognise as Learning.

Track.description: An area Kumo is getting to know you in, or learning to do well, such as sorting your mail, writing as you, your food habits or planning your weekends. Kumo opens one when it starts learning something and moves it by judgement; a correction always steps it back.

note.description: Kumo's line on where it stands, such as "Three weeks of drafts you sent as I wrote them."

confirmed.description: How many times you've confirmed Kumo got it right.

corrected.description: How many times you've corrected it, such as with "That was wrong".

evidence.description: What it stands on, newest first, the latest ten.

TrackEvidence.description: One thing a track stands on: a time you `confirmed` Kumo got it right, `corrected` it, `answered` one of its questions in Understanding you, or Kumo `moved` it to another stage, with why. Show the text alone for a kind you don't recognise.

text.description: In a line, such as "You sent the Tess draft as I wrote it".

stage.description: The stage it moved to, or stepped back to after a correction.

done.description: The call it was about, in Done.

QuestionId.description: Opaque. The server makes it when Kumo adds a question.

QuestionState.description: Where a question stands: `open`, waiting quietly for you for as long as it takes; `answered`, by you; `settled`, Kumo learned the answer elsewhere, such as in the chat, and `note` says where; `dropped`, Kumo let it go because it no longer helps. Treat a state you don't recognise as `dropped`.

Question.description: Something Kumo would like you to explain, in Understanding you, on one of its learning tracks: what it already understands, the missing piece and why it would help. It's optional and quiet: it has no due date, is never overdue, never waits on the Desk and never notifies you. Answer it with a tap on one or more of its `options`, in your own words, written or spoken, or say none fit or you're not sure; "Not now" leaves it open. An answer is enough: Kumo files what it learned in the background and asks nothing more about it.

track.description: The learning track it belongs to, such as Planning with you.

understood.description: What Kumo already understands, from your conversations, memory and sources, in a sentence or two, such as "You keep Sunday mornings free and run long on Saturdays."

missing.description: The missing piece, asked as one question, such as "What makes a weekend feel restful rather than busy?"

why.description: Why it would help, in a line, such as "So the weekends I plan leave you rested, not just full."

options.description: Quick answers to tap: Kumo's honest possibilities, a few words each, for you to recognise or correct. Tap one or several. Empty when only your own words will do.

later_at.description: `open` only: the last time you said "Not now". It stays open, with no reminder; show it after the rest.

unheard.description: `open` only: your spoken answer couldn't be heard, and why, so the question is open for you to answer again.

filed.description: `answered` only, once Kumo has filed it: what it took from your answer, in a line, such as "Weekends start slow: nothing booked before noon."

note.description: `settled`: where Kumo learned the answer, such as "You said in the chat that sleep comes first." `dropped`: why Kumo let it go.

QuestionAnswer.description: Your answer to a question: the options you tapped, your own words, written or spoken, and whether none fit or you're not sure, alone or together.

text.description: Your own words. For a spoken answer, what the server heard, once it has: until then a spoken answer has `audio` and no `text`.

audio.description: A spoken answer: the recording you uploaded, which the server transcribes on its own GPU.

Weekday.description: A day of the week, in your time zone.

WakeUp.description: A time Kumo will wake up and look at something for you: a follow-up, a look after an event, a standing job, or something you asked for. When it comes due, Kumo looks first, then messages you if that's useful, moves it if things changed, or drops it if it's moot, and Done says which. Kumo keeps it current as your life moves, such as a meeting moving or a trip; you can move, change or cancel it too.

at.description: When it's next due, a concrete time Kumo worked out, such as the end of the event it's for.

title.description: What it is in a few plain words, as you'd say it, such as "Ask how the technical went": the line to show in Kumo's plans. A repeating one keeps one title, such as "Look at the week ahead".

what.description: What Kumo will do when it wakes, in its own words, such as "Ask how the Halcyon technical went and note what to work on": show it with `why` when you open a plan.

why.description: Why, in Kumo's words: what it will have in mind when it wakes, such as "It ends at 15:30, and you wanted to talk it through while it's fresh."

by.description: Who made it: `you` asked for it, or `kumo` set it itself. Show one you don't recognise as Kumo's.

motion.description: The thing in motion it's about.

Repeat.description: A wake-up that comes back: on these days, at this time in your time zone, wherever you are, such as weekdays at 09:00.

WakeUpSource.description: Where it came from: your `chat` with Kumo, a `mail` Kumo read, a `calendar` event, or another `wake_up`. Show a kind you don't recognise by its title.

title.description: A line naming it, such as "Tess Harlow: Thursday's technical" or "Halcyon technical, Thu 14:00".

mail.description: `mail` only: the mail, to open in Mail with `message://` and its Message-ID.

event.description: `calendar` only: the event, to open by its uid.

BeliefId.description: Opaque. The server makes it for each belief it checks with you.

Belief.description: Something Kumo believes about you from memory, for you to confirm or correct before it relies on it.

text.description: Such as "You're training for a sub-20 5K".

answer.description: How you answered it: `true`, or `corrected` once Kumo fixed it from your correction.

Onboarding.description: Getting started: Kumo reads your recent mail and calendar and talks with you briefly in the conversation, then shows what it found: beliefs to confirm, bookings it added and what it put in motion.

state.description: `reading` while the catch-up runs, `ready` when the proposal is there, `done` once you've finished getting started.

beliefs.description: With memory from before, a few beliefs to confirm: "Here's what I know. Still true?"

added.description: Future bookings the catch-up put on your calendar.

motions.description: The things the catch-up put in motion, for "Here's what's in motion"; when getting started runs again, everything in motion now.

Problem.description: Something wrong on the server that needs you, shown until it's fixed, when it clears on its own: notifications that can't be sent, a mail or calendar account that keeps failing, a capability that needs setting up, or memory that isn't reaching its backup. A blip that sorts itself out, such as a reconnect, isn't one.

id.description: Stable while it lasts, such as `push` or `mail:outlook`.

area.description: What it's about: `notifications`, `mail`, `calendar`, `contacts`, `capabilities`, `memory`, or `kumo` when its own work in the background can't go on, such as `kumo:paused` while its model's usage limit holds it until a reset. Show an area you don't know plainly.

title.description: One plain line, such as "Notifications can't be sent".

detail.description: What's wrong and what it means for you, in a sentence or two.

fix.description: How to fix it, in plain steps.

ProblemsChanged.title: problems.changed
ProblemsChanged.description: What's wrong on the server changed: a problem appeared, or one was fixed. It carries the whole list, empty once nothing is wrong.

OnboardingChanged.title: onboarding.changed
OnboardingChanged.description: Getting started moved on. It carries the whole state.

RecordingState.description: `queued` while it waits its turn, or for the server's voice to be ready, as `reason` says; `transcribing` while the server listens to it; `ready` once its transcript is; `failed` when it couldn't be transcribed, as `error` says, until it's tried again; `deleted` once its audio and transcript are gone.

Recording.description: A recording you sent in a message, and where its transcript stands. The server transcribes every audio attachment you send, on its own GPU, with times and, as a best guess, who spoke; nothing leaves the server. Fetch the transcript with `GET /v0/recordings/{attachment}/transcript` once it's `ready`.

name.description: The recording's file name, as uploaded.

reason.description: `queued` only: why it hasn't started, such as the voice still loading. Absent while it simply waits its turn.

progress.description: `transcribing` only: how far through it the server is.

done_seconds.description: How much of it has been heard.

total_seconds.description: How long it is, when the server could tell.

speakers.description: `ready` only: how many voices the server told apart, which is a best guess.

RecordingChanged.title: recording.changed
RecordingChanged.description: A recording moved on: queued, transcribing (about every 5% of the way), ready, failed or deleted. It carries the whole recording. These events are compacted like the Desk's, so after a `snapshot`, fetch `GET /v0/recordings` for the recordings you show.

QuestionChanged.title: question.changed
QuestionChanged.description: A question in Understanding you was added or moved on: answered, filed by Kumo, set aside with "Not now", heard, settled or dropped. It carries the whole question, and never notifies. These events are compacted like the Desk's, so after a `snapshot`, fetch `GET /v0/understanding`.

BrowserState.description: What Kumo's browser is doing: `idle`; `browsing`, Kumo at work on a site; `needs_you`, Kumo asked you to take over, for a login, a code, a CAPTCHA or the pay button; `yours`, you hold the page in a takeover and Kumo can't touch it; `waiting`, a commit card waits for your tap. Treat a state you don't recognise as `idle`.

BrowserNeedKind.description: What Kumo needs your hand for: `login` to sign in, `code` for a two-factor code, `captcha`, `payment` to press the site's pay button yourself, or `other`. Treat a kind you don't recognise as `other`.

Browser.description: Kumo's browser on the server: one Chromium, signed in where you signed in, that Kumo uses for you, at iPhone size. A browsing task lives in the thread it started in: show `line` there, in the thread's view or the main chat, and a tap on it peeks at the live view (`GET /v0/capabilities/browser/stream`), which you can take over. Kumo never presses a button that pays, never types a password, card or code, and asks you instead.

line.description: What to show as the task's line, plain words written by the server: "On OpenTable: choosing Sat 19:30 · step 6", "Needs your hand on OpenTable", "You have the page", "Waiting for your OK on OpenTable". Absent while it's idle.

thread.description: The side thread the task lives in. Absent for the main chat, and while idle.

site.description: The site it's on, such as "OpenTable".

url.description: The page's address, without its query.

doing.description: `browsing` only: what Kumo is doing, in its words, such as "choosing Sat 19:30".

step.description: `browsing` only: how many steps Kumo has taken on this task.

need.description: `needs_you`, and `yours` when you took over because Kumo asked: what for. The notification carried the same.

why.description: What to do, in Kumo's words, such as "Sign in to OpenTable so I can book Saturday".

turn.description: The turn that asked, when one did.

lease.description: `yours` only: you hold the page until you hand it back, or until `until`, which every touch moves on; then it goes back to Kumo by itself.

card.description: `waiting` only: the commit card on the Desk.

DreamGroup.description: Where a line of a dream belongs: `planned`, tomorrow put in order (Kumo's blocks and guesses, wake-ups set, moved or dropped); `tidied`, memory tended (pages rewritten, merged, Now kept to what's live); `noticed`, what Kumo noticed or learnt (a lasting lesson on How to help you, a pattern, a chapter); `saved`, kept for you (the day's journal, a message or a question for the morning). Show a group you don't recognise under Noticed.

DreamLine.description: One short line of what a dream did, pointing at what it changed or is about. Lines are in the order Kumo wrote them; group them by `group`.

text.description: Plain words, such as "Moved tomorrow's run to 07:30, before the 09:00 call".

done.description: The entry in Kumo's work for the change this line made, when it made one. Undo it with `POST /v0/done/{entry}/undo` while `undo` is true.

undo.description: Whether `POST /v0/done/{entry}/undo` can take the change back now: it puts the page, the wake-up or the block back as it was before the dream.

page.description: The memory page it changed or is about, such as `memory:journal/2026-11-26`.

wake_up.description: The wake-up it set, moved or dropped; one it dropped is no longer in the plans.

event.description: The item on Kumo's calendar it planned, moved or removed; one it removed is no longer in Coming up.

message.description: A message it posted to you.

Dream.description: One of Kumo's dreams: once a day, at the dream time, Kumo looks back over everything since the last one and puts it in order, then leaves this record. Show it from when it finishes until you've seen it (a moon on the Desk), then as seen.

day.description: The local day it mostly looked back on, such as `2026-11-26` for a dream at 04:00 on the 27th.

trigger.description: `scheduled`, at the dream time (or as soon as the server was back, if it was off then); `manual`, from Dream now.

headline.description: The night in a line, in Kumo's words, such as "A quiet Wednesday: journal written, Thursday planned".

seen_at.description: When you saw it, with `POST /v0/dreams/{dream}/seen`. Until then it's new.

DreamFinished.title: dream.finished
DreamFinished.description: Kumo finished a dream, and left its record. It never notifies: Kumo messages you itself when something from the night is worth it.

BrowserChanged.title: browser.changed
BrowserChanged.description: Kumo's browser changed: a step on a site, a takeover asked for, taken or handed back, a commit card put to you or settled, or the task over. It carries the whole state. These events are compacted like the Desk's, so after a `snapshot`, its `browser` is the state, or idle when absent. They never notify, except that a need notifies once, as a `takeover` notification.

Access.description: How Kumo runs on the server. `sandboxed`, the default: Kumo's commands run in Codex's sandbox, free to write only in Kumo's workspace and to reach the network, and to read the rest of the server. `full`: no sandbox, so its commands can install, restart and change anything the server's user can, Ito's own checkout included, with no approval asked. Either applies from the next turn or piece of work that starts, never to one already running. While it's `full`, show a marker on the chat.

since.description: `full` only: when you turned it on.

AccessChanged.title: access.changed
AccessChanged.description: You turned full access on or off, from any device. It carries the whole state. After a `snapshot`, its `access` is the state, or `sandboxed` when absent. It never notifies.
